stages.summoned: Vellaunos has sent for me. Whatever it is, it has to do with the news from Cenabum.
stages.find_tally: Five years ago Brigodunon gave Rome three hostages: Ateula, Iccios, and my sibling Eponina. If the Cadurci join the revolt, Rome kills or sells them. Vellaunos wants them home before the spring assembly. First I need the Roman tally that says where they were sent. It was kept at the shrine, and it is gone. Cintugnatos the vates knows more.
stages.read_tally: I have the tally back. Nobody in Brigodunon reads Roman letters. Vellaunos says Sulicena, headwoman of Vindomagos, trades with everyone; she may know who can.
stages.ask_riders: Sulicena can't read the tally either. The horsemen holding the ford at the Oltis served in Caesar's cavalry and would know a Roman depot mark. So would Lugurix, the salt merchant in Vindomagos, for a price.
stages.north: The tally was cut at Noviodunum, Caesar's depot on the Liger, in Aedui country. Vellaunos should hear this.
stages.reported: Vellaunos knows. The road goes north, to Noviodunum, and I have to be back before the assembly meets in the spring.
stages.inside: I found them at Noviodunum, in the depot on the Liger: Eponina in the long house by the river, Iccios at the forge, Ateula copying the quartermaster's rolls. The quartermaster is Lucius Orbius, the man who cut our tally. Now to get them out.
stages.freed: All three are out of Noviodunum and on the road home. Now Vellaunos, and the assembly.
stages.freed_some: I got them out of Noviodunum, but not all of them. Ateula stayed. Vellaunos has to hear it from me before the assembly.
stages.left: I left them at Noviodunum. Vellaunos has to hear it from me before the assembly.
stages.done_rising: The assembly of Brigodunon voted to join the revolt. Whatever comes next, it comes for all of us.
stages.done_faith: The assembly of Brigodunon voted to keep faith with Rome, and to sit out the war if Rome and the king will let it.
stages.done_split: The assembly of Brigodunon could not agree. Those who want war will ride with Lucterius; the rest stay home and keep their heads down.
stages.done_late: The assembly met without me and voted to join the revolt. I was somewhere else.

quests.name: The Grotto of the Hanging Dead

stages.start: Someone broke into the shrine and took the offerings and the Roman tally. Cintugnatos thinks it was the outlaws living in the Grotto of the Hanging Dead, northeast of Brigodunon.
stages.pardon_asked: The outlaws are led by Dubnacos, exiled from Brigodunon three winters ago for a killing. He will give back the tally for sixty silver, or for Vellaunos's word that he can come home.
stages.pardon_granted: Vellaunos has agreed to let Dubnacos come home. I should tell him.
stages.done_pardon: Dubnacos gave back the tally and is coming home. Vellaunos gave his word, and so, in a way, did I.
stages.done_bought: I bought the tally back from Dubnacos.
stages.done_lied: I told Dubnacos he was pardoned. He wasn't. He gave me the tally and left the grotto, heading for a home that won't take him.
stages.done_scared: The outlaws fled the grotto and left the tally behind.

stages.start: Sulicena of Vindomagos has twenty sacks of grain promised to Brigodunon, but a band of Germanic horsemen, deserters from Caesar's cavalry, holds the ford at the Oltis and takes a toll from everything that crosses. Their leader is called Haldo.
stages.toll_paid: I paid Haldo's toll. Brigodunon's grain crosses this season. I should tell Sulicena.
stages.riders_gone: I convinced the riders that the Arverni were coming. They rode off. I should tell Sulicena, before anyone finds out there's no army.
stages.riders_recalled: I gave Haldo a forged Roman order promising pardon at Noviodunum. The riders went north to collect it. I should tell Sulicena.
stages.riders_hired: The riders have sworn to ride for Brigodunon when they are called, and have left the ford. I should tell Sulicena.
stages.horses_stolen: I ran off the riders' horses in the night. Men on foot are easier to talk to.
stages.riders_walked: The riders left the ford on foot. I should tell Sulicena.
stages.riders_dead: The riders are dead. I should tell Sulicena.
stages.done: The ford at the Oltis is open and Brigodunon's grain is crossing.

stages.get_spear: Get Old Cottos's grandson's spear back from the bandits by the river.

stages.rumor: Vercingetorix's men are hunting a Roman who kept accounts for a trading house in Gergovia and didn't get out when the news came from Cenabum. Somebody in the lower town is hiding him.
stages.found: The Roman is Paconius, a freedman clerk, passing as Theron's Greek bookkeeper in the lower town. He has his master's tablets and won't let them out of his sight.
stages.tablets: I have the clerk's tablets: Roman accounts, written small and close in Latin. I need someone who can read them, or enough Latin of my own.
stages.read: The tablets are the accounts of the house of Aulus Vettius Calvus, who trades in wine and in people. Brigodunon's three hostages are entered as sold forward: bought from the depot at Noviodunum, to be handed over when the fighting season ends, on account of an Aeduan noble called Dannotalos. Avaricum is in there too, as a line with no number in it yet. Nobody has besieged Avaricum.

stages.start: Ollognatos, the king's hostage-master, wants Brigodunon to send two children of its leading families to Gergovia as hostages, and ten spearmen with them. Rome already has three of ours.
stages.done_pledged: I promised Ollognatos that Brigodunon would send two children and ten spears. Vellaunos doesn't know yet.
stages.done_self: I gave Ollognatos myself as Brigodunon's pledge: my oath to the king in place of two children. If Brigodunon goes back on the revolt, I'm the one who pays.
stages.done_lucterius: I convinced Ollognatos that the Cadurci give hostages as a people, through Lucterius, not hill fort by hill fort. The demand goes to Lucterius. It will come back, but not this month.
stages.done_iron: I paid Brigodunon's levy in silver for iron, and Ollognatos wrote it down as spears. No children this time.
stages.done_vindomagos: I told Ollognatos that Vindomagos is richer than Brigodunon and closer to the road. He sent riders there instead.
stages.done_refused: I told Ollognatos that Brigodunon would give nothing. He cut a notch in a stick and put it behind his ear.

stages.start: Ategnatos, an old noble of the uncle's party, says his son Eppillos is in the pit on the plateau, condemned to burn for sending word to Gobannitio. The king carries out his sentences before he marches. Ategnatos wants his son alive, whatever it costs.
stages.guard_paid: The pit guard will look the other way tonight. I need to be at the pit after dark.
stages.done_spared: The king spared Eppillos the fire. He serves in the front rank now, which may come to the same thing, slower.
stages.done_ears: Eppillos won't burn. He loses his ears instead, and lives, and everyone who sees him will know why.
stages.done_freed: I got Eppillos out of the pit at night. He ran for the hills and his great-uncle. Ategnatos owes me for the rest of his life, if the king doesn't find out how short that is.
stages.done_betrayed: I told Ollognatos that Ategnatos meant to get his son out of the pit. Now there are two of them in it.
stages.failed: The king marched north, and before he went he carried out his sentences. Eppillos burned.

stages.start: Theron of Massilia wants out of Gergovia. A Greek isn't a Roman, but the men hunting Romans aren't good at telling the difference, and he has started to notice them looking. He would travel with someone who can use a spear, if the price were right.
stages.done: Theron travels with me. He reads Latin and Greek, keeps accounts, haggles like a man possessed, and will run at the first sign of a fight. He says this is a sign of intelligence.

stages.rumor: Sumelis in the forum says there is an Aeduan in Avaricum who buys grain and never takes any away. He writes a great deal, she says. The line for Avaricum in the Vettius day book was empty.
stages.found: The Aeduan is Epomeduos, an agent of Dannotalos. He is listing Avaricum's households, and what each would fetch, for when the city falls. He also knows where Brigodunon's three are: at Noviodunum, until the autumn.
stages.done_exposed: I showed Senodonnos what Epomeduos was writing. They took him to the wall. Senodonnos gave me the letter they found on him, Dannotalos's own, for the gate at Noviodunum.
stages.done_turned: Epomeduos works for me now, or says he does. He wrote me into Dannotalos's letter for the gate at Noviodunum as his partner.
stages.done_bought: I bought Dannotalos's letter for the gate at Noviodunum from Epomeduos. He sold it the way he sells everything, without a flicker.
stages.done_killed: Epomeduos is dead. Dannotalos's letter for the gate at Noviodunum was on him.
stages.done_stolen: I have Dannotalos's letter for the gate at Noviodunum, and Epomeduos doesn't.

stages.start: Andecamulos the ironmaster runs the countermines under Avaricum's wall. The Romans are building a terrace against the south wall, and his miners dig under it to bring it down or burn it. He needs hands, ears, pitch, or someone mad enough to go out at night with a torch.
stages.done_dug: I dug in Andecamulos's countermine until I couldn't stand. The drift reached under the terrace.
stages.done_heard: I heard the Roman sappers through the clay and showed the miners where to break in on them.
stages.done_pitch: I brought Andecamulos the pitch for the fire under the terrace.
stages.done_fired: I went out over the wall at night with the picked men and set fire to the Roman sheds. They put it out by morning. They always do.
stages.failed: Avaricum fell before I did anything for the countermine. Nobody is left to ask.

stages.start: Nertomara, a widow of Avaricum, wants her two children taken to her sister at Argentomagus before the Romans close the roads. She won't leave herself: the house was her husband's, and his people are buried by the wall.
stages.boat_paid: Vindos the boatman will take Nertomara's children through the marsh at night. I need to go to him after dark.
stages.done_early: Nertomara's children went south to Argentomagus with a carter, while the road was still open.
stages.done_boat: Vindos poled Nertomara's children through the marsh in the dark, past the Roman pickets. They are on their way to Argentomagus.
stages.done_adit: The miners took Nertomara's children out through their drift under the north wall. They came up in the reeds, and away.
stages.done_runners: The king's runners took Nertomara's children out through the marsh to the camp, and on to Argentomagus.
stages.failed: Avaricum fell, and Nertomara's children were still in it.

stages.start: A girl is hiding in the last granary in the ruins of Avaricum. There is a legionary near the door, and a sentry on the only road out.
stages.done_sneak: I got the girl out of the granary in the dark and through the marsh. She ran toward the king's camp and didn't look back.
stages.done_latin: I told the sentry in Latin that the girl was mine, bought fair, and he waved us through without looking at her. She ran for the marsh as soon as we were past.
stages.done_paid: Thirty silver bought a legionary's back for long enough. The girl is out.
stages.done_vouched: Epomeduos wrote the girl into his book as Aeduan property and walked her past the sentry himself. He sent her toward the marsh. I didn't ask what he wanted for it.
stages.done_fought: I took the girl out of the granary and cut a way through. She's out. I may not be.

stages.start: In Cenabum the townsmen have taken a widow and her small son. Her husband was a freedman of Cita, the Roman grain commissary they killed in the massacre, and somebody wants her dead too before the Romans come back.
stages.done_saved: I got Litumara and her boy out of Cenabum alive.
stages.done_judged: I argued for Litumara before the elder of Cenabum, and the town let her live.
stages.done_bought: I paid Atepomaros for Litumara and her boy: what the Romans had paid for his brother. He took the silver and let them go.
stages.done_given: I gave Litumara up. Her son, too.

stages.start: Caesar is coming to Cenabum. The town has one wooden bridge over the Liger, and when the legions arrive everyone in Cenabum will try to cross it in the same night. Somebody should get the people out before then.
stages.agreed: Senuacos has agreed: when the news comes that Caesar is near, Cenabum goes, by daylight and not by the bridge. I can only hope the news comes in time.
stages.done_saved: I got the people of Cenabum out before the legions came. The town burned anyway, but it burned empty.
stages.done_failed: Caesar came before Cenabum was empty. The bridge was too narrow.

stages.start: The druids of the Carnutes hold Brigodunon's old oath to Rome, sworn when the hostages were given. Senouindos will judge whether Rome has broken it. If Rome has, Brigodunon is free of it.
stages.done_void: The druids have judged: Rome broke faith, and Brigodunon's oath is void. Whatever the assembly decides, it decides free.
stages.done_bound: The druids have judged that the oath still binds. Brigodunon gave its word; Rome has not yet broken its own.
